cards.text: The prophet Jeremiah gets a word from the LORD for all the people of Judah. It's the fourth year of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, which is also the first year of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon. So Jeremiah stands up and speaks to all of Judah and everyone living in Jerusalem.
Jeremiah starts by counting. The LORD's word has been coming to him since the thirteenth year of Josiah, king of Judah, right up to this very day.

cards.question: Jeremiah has been speaking the LORD's word to Judah again and again for ___ years.
All those years of Jeremiah speaking to Judah again and again. How have the people responded?

cards.text: Twenty-three YEARS of the same message, and nobody listening. Friend, that's a group chat where you can SEE the read receipts, and still nothing comes back.
And it's not just Jeremiah. The LORD has sent all His servants the prophets to them, again and again.

cards.question: Jeremiah says the people of Judah listened to the other prophets the LORD sent, just not to him.

cards.text: Here's what all those prophets kept telling them. Turn now, every one of you, from your evil ways and deeds.

cards.question: If the people turned from their evil ways, the prophets said they could stay in the ___ the LORD gave them and their fathers, forever.
The prophets also warned the people of Judah not to follow something, to serve and worship it. What?

cards.text: But the LORD says they didn't listen, and it's to their own harm. It's an oven timer beeping again and again while the whole kitchen yells, "FIVE more minutes!"

cards.question: The LORD says the people of Judah provoked Him to anger with what?

cards.text: Twenty-three years of warnings, and now Jeremiah gets to the "therefore." The LORD of Hosts says, 'Because you have not obeyed My words,' and then He says what He will do.

cards.question: Because Judah has not obeyed, who does the LORD say He will send for?
In this message, the LORD calls Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon 'My servant.'

cards.text: My SERVANT. Nebuchadnezzar, king of BABYLON, along with all the families of the north. I bet nobody in Jerusalem saw that word coming.

cards.question: Who does the LORD say He will bring Nebuchadnezzar against?

answers.text: This land and the nations around it

cards.text: The LORD says He'll make them an object of horror and contempt, an everlasting desolation. Then He names what He'll take away from them.

cards.question: Which of these does the LORD say He will banish from the land?

answers.text: The voices of the bride and bridegroom
The songs of the temple singers
The sound of children at play

cards.text: No sounds of joy, no millstones grinding, no light of the lamp. I know dark from my years in the junk drawer, friend, but this is a whole land becoming a desolate wasteland.

cards.question: The LORD says these nations will serve the king of Babylon for ___ years.

cards.text: Seventy years is a long time to serve somebody. But when those seventy years are complete, the LORD has a word about Babylon itself.

cards.question: When the seventy years are complete, what will the LORD do to the king of Babylon and his nation?
The LORD says the land of the Chaldeans, Babylon's own land, will become an everlasting desolation too.

cards.text: Remember that oven timer? A timer doesn't care how big you are, friend, and when this one goes off, it goes off for the king of Babylon too.
The LORD says He'll bring on that land all the words He has spoken against it, everything written in this book. That's the book of what Jeremiah prophesied against all the nations.

cards.question: Many nations and great kings will enslave Babylon, and the LORD will repay them according to their ___ and the work of their hands.

cards.text: Many nations and great kings will enslave Babylon, and the LORD repays them deed for deed. That's not a vague bill, friend. That's ITEMIZED.

findings.problem: This story card only repeats Jeremiah 25:3, which cards 2 to 4 already covered: 23 years and the people not listening. It adds nothing new from the passage. Its only purpose is the group chat joke, so it is a recap card.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: Two wrong answers start with "Only," so the right answer stands out. "Only the city of Babylon" is also silly: the LORD sending Babylon's king against Babylon makes no sense at this point in the passage, so it isn't believable.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: Jeremiah 25:10 says the LORD will banish "the sounds of joy and gladness." A baker could argue that "The sound of children at play" is one of those sounds, and possibly "The songs of the temple singers" too. So these wrong answers are not clearly false anywhere in the passage.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: This story card adds nothing from the passage. It repeats the punishment of Babylon in 25:12, which cards 11 and 12 already covered, so it is a joke-only recap card.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: The callback changes what the oven timer means. In stop 1, card 11, the timer stood for warnings beeping while people ignored them. Here it stands for a deadline running out on the king of Babylon. The core action in the callback doesn't match its setup, so the joke doesn't click.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: This story card repeats the content of the card 15 question: nations and great kings enslave Babylon, and the LORD repays them according to their deeds. It adds nothing new from 25:14, so it is a recap card that only carries the "ITEMIZED" joke.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.
